mechanism_narrative: A continued easing in workplace and transit suppression signals more daily out-of-home activity, which should lift retail and recreation spending within four weeks. If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep moving toward zero, RETAIL_REC should move up relative to the prior month.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain flat or improve further, but RETAIL_REC is lower over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days, this mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When residential staying-home intensity stops rising and begins easing, discretionary trips resume with a short lag, pushing retail mobility higher over the next two weeks. The mechanism requires RESIDENTIAL to stop increasing week-on-week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL decreases week-on-week after at least two weeks of nondecreasing values
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL declines under the trigger condition and RETAIL_REC does not rise versus the prior two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A joint rebound in transit and workplaces expands the pool of people physically moving through commercial areas, and retail mobility rises only when both series improve together. The effect should show up within one week of the joint improvement.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT rises while WORKPLACES does not, or WORKPLACES rises while TRANSIT does not, and RETAIL_REC still rises materially, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp weakening in park mobility relative to the prior week marks a broader tightening of discretionary movement, which suppresses retail visits over the next month. The signal is directional only when PARKS crosses into a new lower band.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls by at least 3 points week-on-week from an already negative level
failure_condition: If PARKS falls by the stated amount and RETAIL_REC does not decrease relative to the last four weeks, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: When grocery-pharmacy mobility stays comparatively resilient while transit remains depressed, consumers are shifting trips toward necessity channels rather than discretionary shopping, which keeps retail-and-recreation below its recent average over the next two to four weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM stays near its current level while TRANSIT remains weak, but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days, this mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in park visits acts as a proxy for favorable outdoor conditions and general mobility normalization, and this should spill over into higher retail mobility within four weeks. The effect is strongest when PARKS rises for at least two consecutive weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks after a trough
failure_condition: If PARKS rises for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Retail mobility improves only when workplace and transit mobility both accelerate together after a brief lag, because the combined rise indicates commuter traffic spilling into shopping trips. The effect should appear within one week of the acceleration.
failure_condition: If only one of WORKPLACES or TRANSIT improves and RETAIL_REC still increases by the same magnitude as when both improve, the interaction mechanism is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime, a narrowing gap between residential stay-at-home and workplace mobility indicates relaxed constraints and more mixed-purpose trips, which should raise retail-and-recreation over the next two weeks. The signal requires RESIDENTIAL to stop edging up while WORKPLACES stops falling.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES converge in the stated reopening regime but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last two-week mean, the hypothesis fails.
